order.title: MCP Hammer — agent-driven IT AI intake
order.summary: An agent interviews requesters, classifies the completed request and routes it to the right downstream systems. Most downstream systems are mocked, with two real integrations: an Airtable sync that pulls new AI Engagement records into the intake queue, and an Ardoq connector that creates a real Connector Technology Service component when a request is a connector/MCP configuration.

order.title: Org Impact Simulator — workforce scenario planning you can interrogate
order.summary: Pose an external shift — a 20% cut to grant funding lands next quarter — and get a projection grounded in the foundation's own talent history. The reasoning, sample sizes and evidence base are exposed rather than buried, so a headcount planner can challenge the number instead of trusting it. Ships as one self-contained HTML file: no server, no install, no network. A placebo test is built in to show where the method stops holding.

order.title: Strategy Explorer — a defensible strategy briefing, generated on demand
order.summary: A generation engine that queries the Strategic Intelligence Platform graph and renders a self-contained static HTML briefing across the full US Program strategy set. Deliberately not interactive: every figure comes from a query a person reviewed, and inferred or proxied values stay visually distinguishable from retrieved fact, so the artifact survives the first reviewer who knows the portfolio.

order.title: Partner meeting prep, drafted from the record
order.summary: Preparing for a partner meeting means reading across portfolio records and years of accumulated documents in a shared folder, and the details that matter most — a finance function that has stalled, a figure that disagrees with itself between two records, a document promised and never delivered — are exactly the ones that get missed. This drafts three artifacts from those two sources: a program officer brief with the questions to ask ranked by importance, a leadership update, and a partner-facing brief. Every claim cites the record or filename it came from, and it states plainly what it did not read, so the gaps are visible rather than silent.

order.title: Stakeholder reporting and data updating redesign
Reclass Intake — the reclass workbook as a form that knows the rules
order.summary: A reclass request today is hand-transcribed into a workbook and emailed. Paste a transaction key, it is fetched live from Power BI, check which fields change, pick new values from dropdowns where invalid targets cannot be selected. 16 business rules run as you type, each citing the document it came from, and out comes the exact Working List file accounting already consumes.

order.title: KB Queens — an AI Knowledge-Base generator for INVEST and Salesforce Support
order.summary: Support teams sit on a goldmine of failure data — Jira stories, linked bugs, QA defects, Salesforce metadata. Writing KB articles from it by hand takes hours per feature and quality depends on who wrote it. This mines that evidence automatically and drafts articles in a consistent format in minutes, walking a 14-category failure taxonomy and citing a Jira key or metadata component for every step. Draft only: everything goes to SME review before an agent sees it.

order.title: whiteboard → sprint
order.summary: Turns whiteboard photos and meeting transcripts into Jira issues — but interrogates the ambiguities before writing anything. Sprint notes are full of shorthand that only made sense in the room: an arrow between two boxes, "someone should look at it", a name with no due date. This reads the photo or transcript, asks the specific questions a PM would ask before filing anything ambiguous, and only then writes tickets — sized, with acceptance criteria — straight to Jira. .NET 10 / C# 14 backend, React and Vite frontend.
